output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Monday casuals pay and Kisumu loading, Embakasi

Brian,

This is the briefing for Monday. I am leaving it as a draft tonight so I can read it once more before I sleep. Unless I message you otherwise, treat it as final for Sunday.

First, the tone. Go in calm and straightforward, not defensive. The guys did nothing wrong. This is our mess. Lead with the apology and the facts, not with what they need to do for us.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED WITH FRIDAY’S PAY

Friday’s bulk payment file was rejected by the bank. The reason was a file-format issue. After the bank’s platform upgrade on 25 November, our old template no longer worked. Column 7 — beneficiary reference — was longer than the 20-character limit. No payments in that file were processed.

Finance only saw the rejection after 5pm, after the bank cut-off. That is why no one was paid on Friday. It was not because the casuals did anything wrong, and it was not because their money was not due. It is our error.

We are not trying to run the same file again. The payment is being moved to M-Pesa bulk. Njeri has approved that, and approved the KES 500 per head for lunch and fare, plus the M-Pesa charges on the company. Peninah has 198 numbers confirmed and 14 she could not reach, mostly the new loaders from the Athi River intake.

WHEN THE MONEY LANDS

For the 198 confirmed numbers, the commitment is M-Pesa by 11am Monday. Not earlier. Kevin has been clear he will not promise before 11, and I am not going to let us repeat Mombasa 2024. You remember: the supervisor told them “by lunch”, money came at 4pm, half the shift sat down. We do not give a time we cannot keep. 11am is the time. If it slips, we tell them immediately; we do not let 11 pass in silence.

The 14 unreachable numbers: Peninah will be at Embakasi from 7:30 with the printout. Those guys must see her first thing and give correct numbers face to face. Once the number is confirmed, finance will push the payment. Do not promise the 14 a specific time until Peninah has the correct number. Do tell them they are not forgotten and will be paid.

KES 500 per head for lunch and fare is for every casual on the affected list, paid in the same M-Pesa batch as their pay. The M-Pesa charges are on the company, not deducted from anyone. That is approved; say it plainly.

Peninah can print payslips on the spot for anyone who wants one. Tell them that.

WHAT YOU CAN PROMISE

1. A direct apology from management, in person, first thing. You are giving it. No excuses, no blaming the bank in front of them. “We missed Friday. That was our failure. I’m sorry.” That is the opening.
2. M-Pesa payment by 11am Monday for the 198 confirmed numbers. For the 14, payment after Peninah captures the correct number — same day, but no fixed time until the number is confirmed.
3. KES 500 per head lunch and fare, same batch as their pay, charges on the company.
4. Peninah at the gate from 7:30 for numbers and payslips.
5. Nobody on the affected list is being dropped. Every casual on that list will be paid.
6. No one will be dismissed or threatened with dismissal on Monday. That is the procedure, not a favour.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT PROMISE OR SAY

Do not give any time earlier than 11am. Not “by 8”, not “by 9”, not “by lunch”. If someone pushes you, say: “The committed time is 11am. I won’t lie to you with an earlier time.” Then stop.

Do not say the bank has released the money, that it is “in your account”, or that it is “processing” unless you have confirmed it. Friday’s file was rejected; it was never paid.

Do not promise physical payment at the gate or a bank transfer. It is M-Pesa.

Do not promise extra money beyond the KES 500, permanent contracts, or that this will never happen again. If they ask for more, say you will take it back to HR, but you are not negotiating compensation at the gate.

Do not discuss internal finance details. If they ask why, keep it to: “The payment file was rejected because our format was out of date. Finance has moved it to M-Pesa. Peninah is handling numbers.” That is enough. Anything beyond that is not for the depot.

Do not threaten contracts, dismissal, or sending anyone home. The procedure says no dismissal or threat of dismissal on the day. Do not let a supervisor do it either.

OUMA AND THE KISUMU TRUCKS

Ouma is loud, but he is not a bad man. He has four kids and rent due. Do not go in treating him as the ringleader. Before you address the whole group, get Joseph’s update, then take Ouma aside privately. Hear him out. Acknowledge the rent and the fact that Friday hurt. Then give him the facts: M-Pesa by 11 for confirmed numbers, Peninah at 7:30 for the 14, KES 500 lunch and fare, charges on us. Ask him to help you get the trucks loaded while the payment runs. Ask him what he needs to hear to calm the group. Do not offer side deals, and do not promise him anything different from what is in this note.

If Ouma’s group refuses to load the Kisumu trucks, do not stand there arguing in front of everyone and do not turn it into a showdown. Treat it as a stoppage and follow the joint Ops/HR procedure:

A stoppage is not a grievance channel. Grievances go to the shift supervisor, then HR within 48 hours. But do not hide behind that on Monday. Their pay complaint is real; fix the pay and hear them.

Any stoppage is handled by Operations and HR together. That means you and me, not a supervisor alone. Since I will be travelling, call me before I board. I am up from 4:30. WhatsApp me if anything changes. If I am already in the air, leave a clear message and copy Njeri. Do not make a unilateral decision on discipline or dismissal.

No one is to be dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day. No warnings, no contract talk. Keep it factual.

Keep Joseph with the group. Ask him to note the time the refusal starts and who spoke for the group. Keep the gate calm. Do not let a crowd form around you.

Keep the 9am departure in view. Kisumu trucks have to leave by 9 or we miss the offloading slot at the mill. If loading has not started and the refusal is holding, tell dispatch/transport early, not at 8:45. They need to manage the mill slot. Do not promise the mill or the drivers a new time unless dispatch confirms it.

If the trucks cannot load, say clearly: “The pay issue is being fixed. This stoppage will be handled by Operations and HR together. No one is being dismissed today.” Then step back and call me.

MONDAY TIMETABLE

5:30 — you at depot. Get Joseph’s update first. Do not walk into the crowd cold.

6:00–6:30 — find Ouma privately if you can. Apologise, give facts, ask him to load.

7:30 — Peninah at the gate with the list and the 14 names. Announce that anyone not yet confirmed should see her before starting. Payslips printed on request.

Before I board — WhatsApp me with the temperature: Ouma, the group, the trucks. I will have my phone on from 4:30.

11:00 — M-Pesa commitment for confirmed numbers. If there is any delay, tell the group immediately and tell me.

Brian, I know you will want to fix this on the spot. Don’t improvise on the money. You have Joseph for the floor and Peninah for the numbers. Your job is to apologise, tell the truth, keep it calm, and escalate the stoppage. I am sorry I won’t be there. We have worked together six years; I would not hand this to anyone else.

Achieng
